kid: Home internet was a phone call. The computer’s modem rang the internet company, beeping and screeching, and while you were online, nobody could use the phone.
nerd: Dial-up: a modem at 28.8 kbit/s (56k came in 1997; V.90 in 1998) calls the ISP’s modem bank, and PPP gives the PC its own public address. No Wi‑Fi, no router, no NAT.

describe.kid: A big beige computer with a deep screen, and a keyboard on a cable. Its modem sits on a shelf, blinking, and phones the internet company.
describe.nerd: A desktop PC: its external modem dials the ISP on the phone line, with no router in between.

street.nerd: Out and about in 1995, GSM could carry data: a 9.6 kbit/s circuit-switched call (CSD) from a phone with a cable to a laptop. Far too slow for video.
